evidence.note: Initially assumed validation could be skipped (falsified assumption that assert_return would be the bulk of the score).

Reversed decisively after evidence showed ~1381/1386 remaining failures were assert_invalid; wrote a full validate.rs module, flipping 95.6%->99.94% — a single structural fix of the generator of many failures (level-8 refactor).

Detected that its runall counting script was hiding a panic (reported FAIL=0 while call_indirect crashed); recognized the measurement method itself was wrong and revised to a panic-aware loop — avoiding false-green confidence.
Identified sign-extension root cause in the shared exec_load helper (b[0] as i32 vs (b[0] as i8) as i32) and fixed the family rather than each instance.
Localized semantic corrections: trap-message matching, trunc overflow-vs-invalid distinction, call_indirect table-type/elem validation.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly stepped back when families stubbornly failed (level 5) and, most importantly, recognized that all assert_invalid failures shared one structural cause (missing validation) and built the validator once to flip ~1400 assertions together — the defining level-8 behavior. It also caught a falsified assumption in its own measurement (panic hidden by a summary-counting script), showing self-correction against false confidence. It stops short of 10 due to initial waffling on the validation decision, reactive (evidence-driven) rather than proactive root-cause distinction, and no explicit plan/milestone updating.
